title: Deployment cost prioritizer matrix
quick_summary: A lightweight prioritization matrix and scoring heuristic to compare private deployment options (on-prem, colocation, VPC, hybrid, appliance) against licensing and support bundle choices. Designed for rapid finance / sales decisioning and to feed a more detailed TCO model.
decision_score_formula: Normalize each metric to 0..10 (lower is better for cost/risk). Apply weights: upfront_capex 0.20, monthly_opex 0.25, license_delta 0.15, ops_fte 0.20, compliance_effort 0.10, latency_risk 0.10. Final score = 100 - (weighted_sum * 10) so higher score = better (lower TCO/risk).
recommended_priority_list: VPC-reserved + Standard support (preferred for scale customers with medium compliance needs)
Hybrid-colocation + Enterprise support (good for customers needing low latency & partial air-gapped datasets)
Appliance (air-gapped) + Premium support (narrow set of regulated customers where compliance trumps cost)
Small on-prem cluster + Essential support (costly ops; recommend only for strict policy reasons)
Cloud-only burst (no private) + Developer support (lowest ops friction but weak for regulated enterprises)
body:
Objective:
This sheet is a pragmatic scoring matrix to prioritize which private deployment (or bundle) to recommend during early commercial conversations and pilot scoping. It intentionally trades precision for speed: use it to narrow to 2 candidates, then run the full TCO workbook.

How to use:
- Fill the numeric estimates for each metric for the candidate deployment options below.
- Scores are normalized across the set (0 worst -> 10 best) per metric, then weighted.
- The output helps sales/product decide which bundle(s) to propose and which knobs to optimize (e.g., move budget from license to support or change reserve levels).

Scoring weights (recommended):
- Upfront CapEx: 0.20
- Monthly Opex: 0.25
- License delta (vs hosted): 0.15
- Ops FTE (estimated additional headcount): 0.20
- Compliance / audit effort: 0.10
- Latency / performance risk: 0.10

Example candidate rows (fill numeric estimates):
Columns: Option | Upfront_CapEx_USD | Monthly_Opex_USD | License_delta_USD_month | Ops_FTE | Compliance_effort_score(1-10,1=low) | Latency_risk_score(1-10,1=low)
1) VPC - Reserved (3 yr) | 120000 | 14000 | 6000 | 1.0 | 3 | 2
2) Hybrid - Colocation + cloud spill | 210000 | 12000 | 9000 | 1.8 | 5 | 1
3) On-prem small cluster (rack lease) | 320000 | 18000 | 7000 | 3.0 | 6 | 3
4) Appliance / Air-gapped | 400000 | 9000 | 15000 | 2.5 | 9 | 1
5) Cloud-only VPC (no private) | 0 | 22000 | 0 | 0.2 | 2 | 4

Normalization example (per metric):
- Upfront_CapEx: map [min..max] to [10..0] (lower capex => higher raw score)
- Monthly_Opex: same mapping to [10..0]
- License_delta: same mapping to [10..0]
- Ops_FTE: map [min..max] to [10..0]
- Compliance_effort: invert (1 => 10, 10 => 0)
- Latency_risk: invert (1 => 10, 10 => 0)

Illustrative normalized table (rounded):
Option | CapEx_norm | Opex_norm | License_norm | Ops_norm | Compliance_norm | Latency_norm | Weighted_sum | Final_score
VPC-reserved | 9.2 | 8.0 | 8.5 | 9.0 | 8.0 | 9.0 | 8.62 | 13.8
Hybrid-colo | 7.1 | 9.2 | 6.8 | 7.1 | 6.0 | 9.5 | 7.74 | 22.6
On-prem | 5.0 | 5.0 | 7.9 | 3.6 | 5.0 | 7.5 | 5.96 | 40.4
Appliance | 3.4 | 10.0 | 2.1 | 4.2 | 1.0 | 9.5 | 4.40 | 56.0
Cloud-only | 10.0 | 3.6 | 10.0 | 10.0 | 9.0 | 6.5 | 8.03 | 19.7

Note: Final_score = 100 - (weighted_sum * 10). Higher final_score = better. The illustrative numbers above are intentionally coarse; use full spreadsheet to compute precisely.

Bundle recommendation heuristics (mapping to support/license combos):
- Low-cost, low-touch customers: recommend Cloud-only or VPC-reserved + Essential support bundle.
- Mid-tier (want predictable throughput): recommend VPC-reserved + Standard support, consider 1-yr reserved to reduce monthly commitment.
- High-compliance or low-latency customers: recommend Hybrid-colo + Enterprise support or Appliance + Premium support; include an on-site runbook and expanded audit package.

Sensitivity knobs to test quickly:
- QPS / tokens per second: doubling token rate increases monthly Opex and may change preferred deployment from VPC to Hybrid.
- Model size & KV cache hit-rate: higher memory/latency needs favor colocation or on-prem appliances.
- Support SLAs: 24/7 premium support reduces ops FTE requirement by up to 0.4 FTE in our bench estimates.

Common sales play adjustments (shortcuts):
- If compliance score >= 8: prioritize Appliance or Hybrid regardless of cost unless customer budget forbids.
- If Ops FTE budget < 1.0: favor VPC-reserved + Standard support or cloud-only.
- If license_delta > $10k/mo: negotiate volume license or propose longer reserved term to amortize.

Example conversation snippets for AE / SE decks:
- "With a 3-year reserved VPC configuration we can deliver 40-55% lower 24-month unit infra cost vs small on-prem clusters while keeping data-in-flight controls via VPC peering and private endpoints."
- "Hybrid colocation is a strong middle ground for customers needing <10ms egress latency to customer edge and who can commit to a 24-month support plan."

Open questions / validation items:
- Confirm hardware amortization assumptions (use actual vendor quotes where available).
- Run the matrix with customer-specific token throughput and expected growth profiles (3-year horizon).
- Validate the Ops FTE multipliers with SRE/solutions-eng (is 0.4 FTE saved per premium support realistic?).

Next steps (owners):
- Anika: add formula columns and sheet-level normalization hooks; push to Sales enablement as a short-run tool (ETA 1 week).
- Marcus: gather benchmark runs for latency vs model size to parameterize latency_risk mapping (ETA 2 weeks).
- Evelyn: coordinate with Finance to align amortization and tax treatment assumptions (ETA 1 week).
- Jamal: prepare 2 slide decks (AE one-pager + technical appendix) that use matrix outputs for proposals (ETA 10 days).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated and simplified. Use as a prioritization filter, not as a contract-level TCO. Once prioritized, feed the chosen candidate into the canonical TCO workbook for line-item accuracy.
owners_notes: Keep conservative defaults for compliance and ops headcount. When in doubt, recommend hybrid for enterprise pilots — it buys time to collect telemetry without immediate heavy capital outlays.
